claim_text: 來源機構：Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society (AAAI)；資料標題：Culturally Situated AI Safety for Youth: Saudi Arabian Perspectives of Youth, Parents and Teachers；來源刊登日：2026-10-11。作者摘要報告：分析 736 則 Reddit 與 1,262 則 X 貼文，並訪談 31 名沙烏地阿拉伯受訪者（7–17 歲兒少 8 人、家長 13 人、教師 10 人），探討兒少、家長與教師使用生成式 AI 的經驗與風險認知；作者指出，兒少向生成式 AI 揭露個人與家庭資訊（尤其在尋求情緒支持時）帶有明顯風險，且與當地重視端莊、隱私與名譽的文化期待相衝突。（AI 輔助摘要，未經真人逐則審稿；請參閱原文。）
source_title: Culturally Situated AI Safety for Youth: Saudi Arabian Perspectives of Youth, Parents and Teachers
title_zh: 文化情境化的兒少 AI 安全：沙烏地阿拉伯兒少、家長與教師的觀點

original_excerpt: this study explores youth's (aged 7-17), parents' and teachers' interactions with GenAI tools and risk perceptions through a non-Western lens. … We analyzed 736 Reddit psots, and 1,262 X (Twitter) posts, and conducted interviews with 31 Saudi Arabian participants (8 youth, 13 parents, 10 teachers). … We found significant risks tied to youth’s disclosure of personal and family information, which conflict with culturally rooted expectations of modesty, privacy, and honor, particularly when youth seek emotional support from GenAI.

summary_evidence_spans: this study explores youth's (aged 7-17), parents' and teachers' interactions with GenAI tools and risk perceptions through a non-Western lens.
We analyzed 736 Reddit psots, and 1,262 X (Twitter) posts, and conducted interviews with 31 Saudi Arabian participants (8 youth, 13 parents, 10 teachers).

We found significant risks tied to youth’s disclosure of personal and family information, which conflict with culturally rooted expectations of modesty, privacy, and honor, particularly when youth seek emotional support from GenAI.

claim_text: 來源機構：Eurasia Journal of Mathematics, Science and Technology Education (Modestum)；資料標題：Teachers’ perceptions of ChatGPT support across TPACK domains: A cross-sectional survey in UAE schools；來源刊登日：2026-10-11。作者摘要報告：以橫斷式問卷調查阿聯 109 名在職教師對 ChatGPT 支援教學的看法，涵蓋 TPACK 七個知識面向；教師認為 ChatGPT 在各面向都提供正面支援，內容知識得分最高、科技知識最低。作者建議教師專業發展著重提示設計、批判評估 AI 產出、偏誤意識、隱私保護與合乎倫理的使用。（AI 輔助摘要，未經真人逐則審稿；請參閱原文。）
source_title: Teachers’ perceptions of ChatGPT support across TPACK domains: A cross-sectional survey in UAE schools
title_zh: 教師對 ChatGPT 在各 TPACK 領域支援之知覺：阿拉伯聯合大公國學校之橫斷面調查
source_organization: Eurasia Journal of Mathematics, Science and Technology Education (Modestum)
source_locator: 出版者文章頁：Publication date: 11 Oct 2026；Volume 22, Issue 11, Article No: em2948；citation_publication_date 2026-10-11；全文 PDF：Received 08 June 2026、Accepted 02 October 2026；Abstract；摘要歸屬：文章頁 Abstract 第 2、4、5、9 句
original_excerpt: A quantitative cross-sectional survey design was employed, with data collected from 109 in-service teachers in the United Arab Emirates using a structured questionnaire measuring seven TPACK knowledge domains. … The results indicate that teachers perceived ChatGPT as providing positive support across all TPACK domains. … Content knowledge (CK) received the highest score, particularly for curriculum development, lesson planning, and instructional content preparation, whereas technological knowledge (TK) received the lowest score. … The study recommends professional development focusing on prompt design, critical evaluation of AI-generated content, bias awareness, privacy protection, and ethical AI use.
interpretation_note: 轉述作者摘要的設計、對象與描述性結果；屬教師看法調查，非實際教學成效。
scope_limitation: 同儕審查期刊論文（EJMSTE，J50，管理者 2026-10-12 決定加入監測清單）；對象為經阿聯一所大學研究所課程招募的 109 名在職中小學教師（全文：93.6% 任教私校）；教師自評看法，不涉及成效。

ai_lit_note: 研究在職教師以 TPACK 框架看 ChatGPT 對教學的支援（AI-TPACK），對應 T-TEA「整合AI與教學法」與 T-BAS「選用適性適規之AI工具」
summary_evidence_spans: A quantitative cross-sectional survey design was employed, with data collected from 109 in-service teachers in the United Arab Emirates using a structured questionnaire measuring seven TPACK knowledge domains.
The results indicate that teachers perceived ChatGPT as providing positive support across all TPACK domains.

Content knowledge (CK) received the highest score, particularly for curriculum development, lesson planning, and instructional content preparation, whereas technological knowledge (TK) received the lowest score.
The study recommends professional development focusing on prompt design, critical evaluation of AI-generated content, bias awareness, privacy protection, and ethical AI use.
